proposals.risk: a result its requirement or criteria name is computed or chosen wrongly
proposals.rationale: Only the newly-added tool steps are used when building the tool result message's context and the state records the previous tool state, so the tool result round-trip loses accumulated steps and the tool trace/state is not advanced.

proposals.risk: a result its requirement or criteria name is computed or chosen wrongly
proposals.rationale: The tool-result message is built from all steps accumulated so far rather than only the steps produced in this round, so earlier tool results (e.g. the add result) are re-sent on the next turn and duplicated, corrupting the round-trip before the multiply step.

proposals.risk: one input partition its requirement or criteria name is no longer handled as they say
proposals.rationale: Tool results are appended only for the latest round's steps but the message builder no longer gets the tool_choice reset; instead the tool_choice is never advanced, so forced tool choice repeats every round and the workflow never reaches a final response.

proposals.risk: one input partition its requirement or criteria name is no longer handled as they say
proposals.rationale: When the tool round limit is reached the response is built from the pre-round state's trace, and more importantly the results of tool rounds are fed back using all steps instead of only new ones, so previously executed tool results (add) are re-sent in later turns duplicating round-trip messages for multi-step workflows.

proposals.risk: an order or a before/after boundary its requirement names is broken
proposals.rationale: Tool-result messages are appended using the previous tool state's steps for the 'all_steps' context and the new-step slice is computed from the wrong boundary, so the provider receives stale/duplicated results instead of only the newly executed round's results.

proposals.risk: an order or a before/after boundary its requirement names is broken
proposals.rationale: The tool state is not advanced when the round limit is reached and the final response uses the pre-round trace; also the tool_choice is not updated after a round (the original plan choice is kept), so forced tool choice would persist and the workflow can never reach a final answer after tool results.

proposals.risk: an external interaction its requirement rules out happens anyway
proposals.rationale: The tool-round limit check is evaluated against the state from before the current round, so the limit is only noticed one round late. This allows an extra local tool execution and an extra provider turn beyond the configured limit.

proposals.risk: an external interaction its requirement rules out happens anyway
proposals.rationale: When the tool round limit is reached, the function logs it but then no longer stops: it appends the tool results and returns a continuing state without a response. The loop then makes another provider call even though the limit forbids it.
